description: Embark on a culinary journey to Oaxaca with this authentic Mole Negro, a masterpiece of Mexican cuisine. This complex black mole boasts layers of smoky chiles, rich spices, and a hint of chocolate, creating an unparalleled depth of flavor. Perfect for a special dinner, it transforms any meal into a memorable feast.

instructions.title: Prepare and Rehydrate Chiles
instructions.text: Carefully wipe the dried chiles clean. Heat a dry comal or skillet over medium heat and toast each chile for 20-30 seconds per side until fragrant but not burnt. Remove stems and seeds. Place the toasted chiles in a bowl, cover with hot water, and let them rehydrate for at least 20 minutes, or until soft. Drain, reserving the soaking liquid.

instructions.title: Roast Aromatics and Fry Plantain
instructions.text: On a baking sheet, roast the tomatillos, Roma tomatoes, onion, and garlic at 400F (200C) for 15-20 minutes, or until softened and slightly charred. In a separate pan, heat 1 tablespoon of lard or oil and fry the sliced plantain until golden brown. Set aside all roasted and fried ingredients.

instructions.title: Toast Spices, Nuts, Seeds, and Bread
instructions.text: In a clean, dry skillet over medium-low heat, toast the almonds, peanuts, sesame seeds, and pumpkin seeds separately until lightly golden and fragrant. Be careful not to burn them. In the same skillet, briefly toast the cinnamon stick, cloves, black peppercorns, cumin seeds, and anise seeds until aromatic. Add the torn tortillas and bread pieces to the skillet and toast until crisp. Set aside.

instructions.title: Blend All Ingredients for the Paste
instructions.text: Combine the rehydrated chiles, roasted tomatillos, tomatoes, onion, garlic, fried plantain, toasted nuts, seeds, spices, tortillas, bread, and raisins in a blender. Add 2 cups of chicken broth and blend until a very smooth paste forms. You may need to do this in batches. If the paste is too thick, add a little more reserved chile soaking liquid or broth. Pass the blended mixture through a fine-mesh sieve to ensure a silky texture, pressing down on solids and discarding any fibrous material.

instructions.title: Fry the Mole Paste
instructions.text: Heat 3 tablespoons of lard or oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Once hot, carefully pour in the strained mole paste. Cook, stirring constantly, for 20-30 minutes, allowing the paste to darken and thicken. This step is crucial for developing the mole's deep flavor and color.

instructions.title: Simmer and Finish the Mole
instructions.text: Gradually stir in the remaining chicken broth, about 1 cup at a time, bringing the mixture to a gentle simmer after each addition. Add the chopped Mexican chocolate, sugar, and salt. Continue to simmer the mole, stirring occasionally, for at least 70 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the sauce to thicken to your desired consistency. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.

instructions.title: Serve with Chicken
instructions.text: Serve the rich Oaxacan Black Mole hot over cooked chicken pieces. Garnish with a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds. It pairs wonderfully with white rice and warm corn tortillas. Enjoy this traditional Mexican masterpiece!

tips: For the most authentic flavor, use a comal or cast-iron skillet to toast your chiles and spices; this brings out their deep aromas without burning.
If Chilhuacle Negro chiles are available, substitute them for some of the Pasilla Oaxaca to achieve a truly traditional Oaxacan flavor profile.
Mole Negro tastes even better the next day as flavors deepen. Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days, or freeze for up to 3 months.
